needsHuman.title: Kids always have control
needsHuman.reason: Every play/fail/win screenshot shows only a "Home (hold)" button; no mute or pause icon is visible on these screens, and the Sound toggle in the source lives in Settings.js behind the "Grown-ups (hold)" gate on the Home screen rather than being reachable from within play, so it's unclear a child can mute sound without an adult's help mid-game.

rules.title: No blood
rules.reason: No blood, splatter or red gore anywhere; the red balls, red track trim and red hazards read as normal game colour.

rules.title: No weapons or guns
rules.reason: No weapons are shown or used to attack anyone; track pieces named "Swinging hammer" and "Wrecking ball" (e.g. the "Hammer Time" level) are static/moving course obstacles like Mazle's approved spike, not weapons wielded against characters.

rules.title: No bashing or breaking of living things
rules.reason: Nothing animate is bashed or broken; only balls rolling on tracks, ramps, gaps and plain obstacles are shown, none with faces.

rules.title: No injury or death shown
rules.reason: Falling through a gap just poofs/respawns the ball back at the last checkpoint with no wound, body, or death wording shown.

rules.title: No harm to animals or creatures
rules.reason: No animals or creatures appear in any screen or text; nothing is hunted, trapped or harmed.

rules.title: No scary content
rules.reason: All scenes are brightly lit (blue sky, green grass, sunny sky-road) with cheerful balls; nothing dark, threatening or jump-scare-like appears.

rules.title: No meanness
rules.reason: No insulting or mocking text appears anywhere in the UI strings or screenshots; only neutral labels like "Go!", "FINISH", "Place 1".

rules.title: No stereotypes
rules.reason: Characters are plain colourful balls with no ethnic, gender or group-based caricature or jokes.

rules.title: No romance, sexual content, drugs, alcohol, tobacco or vaping
rules.reason: No romance, sexual content, or drug/alcohol/tobacco/vape imagery; hearts are not used at all in the shown UI.

rules.title: No bad language
rules.reason: No swearing or crude insults in any visible or source text; only friendly labels like "Go!" and "FINISH".

rules.title: No dangerous stunts a kid could copy
rules.reason: The only "risky" action is a ball rolling along a clearly fantastical floating sky track, which is the rubric's explicit OK example, not a copyable real-world stunt.

rules.title: No gambling or casino-style mechanics
rules.reason: The "World code" emoji entry (🍇🦀⚽🐮) with a dice-style icon and "New world" button is a shareable seed for generating a playground layout, not a chance-based prize; no loot boxes, spins-for-reward or betting appear.

rules.title: No money, ads or data
rules.reason: No prices, purchases, ads, sign-in, or personal-info fields appear; the only settings are local (world code, ball skins) with no link out of the game visible.

rules.title: No manipulative design
rules.reason: The race countdown (3,2,1,GO!) is a normal start cue, and results/finish screens offer a clear "Play again"/Home choice with no streaks, timers-to-return, or guilt-trip prompts.

rules.title: Safe for the senses
rules.reason: Win screens show colourful confetti at a steady rate, not strobing; no red/white flash or single-frame flash pattern is evident, and no sound spike is indicated in the notes.

rules.title: Kids always have control
rules.reason: Every play/fail/win screenshot shows only a "Home (hold)" button; no mute or pause icon is visible on these screens, and the Sound toggle in the source lives in Settings.js behind the "Grown-ups (hold)" gate on the Home screen rather than being reachable from within play, so it's unclear a child can mute sound without an adult's help mid-game.

checks.title: Reading needed
checks.reason: All visible instruction/button text is short ("Grown-ups (hold)", "Level 4: Hammer Time", "World code" — all ≤4 words), satisfying the word-count half of the threshold. But the audio_with_text requirement is not met: source analysis shows no speechSynthesis and no voice-over audio files, so early readers who can't decode labels like "Level 2: Bumpy Road" or the Playground setup category names have no spoken fallback.

checks.title: Spoken, replayable instructions
checks.reason: Sound analysis confirms speechSynthesis is not used and no narrated audio files back the UI; only WebAudio (sound effects) is present. Early readers have no spoken, replayable instructions for menus (e.g. Playground setup's many category buttons) or in-game hints.

checks.title: Time pressure
checks.reason: Race mode has a visible 3-2-1-GO countdown and simultaneous opponent balls racing toward a finish line with live placement ("1st") shown — genuine competitive time pressure. It's an optional mode (Playground/Test Track have none), which softens this, but it isn't "gentle-optional" pressure within Race itself.

checks.title: Failing
checks.reason: Falling through a track gap has no lose message or scary text — the ball simply drops (failing-gap-fall.png) and reappears at the last checkpoint on the track (failing-respawn.png) with the same minimal HUD, consistent with a soft, fast reset.

checks.title: Things on screen at once
checks.reason: Actual gameplay screens are clean (just the Home button and the ball), but the Playground setup screen presents Back plus 3 size options, 2 surfaces, 3 terrains, 5 features, 3 star-density options, a world-code panel, and a Go button simultaneously — far above the 5-6 target for this bracket, even though it's a setup screen rather than live play.

checks.title: Scariness
checks.reason: Higher levels are named "Hammer Time" and "Going Big" and include pieces like "Swinging hammer" and "Wrecking ball." The setup thumbnails render them as small, cartoonish grey/red shapes rather than menacing, but no in-motion gameplay screenshot of these obstacles was provided, so intensity for the youngest bracket can't be fully confirmed.

checks.title: Contrast
checks.reason: Text consistently uses bold dark outlines or white-on-saturated-color styling (e.g. yellow "Rolly Bally" title with black outline on sky blue, white labels on solid green/red/blue buttons). Selected options in setup screens are marked with a thicker border, not color alone.

checks.title: Reading needed
checks.reason: All on-screen text (button labels, level names, setup categories, "FINISH", "GO!", place badges) is single words or short 2-4 word phrases using common vocabulary — well under a grade 3 reading level.

checks.title: Spoken, replayable instructions
checks.reason: Spoken instructions are only recommended for this bracket, and none are present — the game relies entirely on icon/text buttons and short labels, which is acceptable for readers at this level but a missed nicety.

checks.title: Time pressure
checks.reason: Countdown starts and racing against opponent balls for placement is well within what's allowed for this bracket, and Race remains an optional mode alongside the untimed Playground and Test Track.

checks.title: Failing
checks.reason: Same soft checkpoint-respawn behavior comfortably clears the more permissive lives-ok threshold for this bracket; no penalty screen or life-loss messaging was observed.

checks.title: Things on screen at once
checks.reason: The Playground setup screen has on the order of 18-19 simultaneous buttons/panels (size, surface, terrain, 5 features, star density, world code, Go, Back), exceeding the max of 8 for this bracket; Race setup (5 level cards + 4 race-length chips + Go/Back) is similarly dense.

checks.title: Scariness
checks.reason: Named hazards like "Swinging hammer" and "Wrecking ball" read as mechanical obstacle-course elements in bright, low-poly cartoon style — well within mild fantasy-conflict/obstacle territory for this bracket.

checks.title: Contrast
checks.reason: Same outlined/high-contrast text treatment holds throughout menus, HUD, and results screens, and selection state is conveyed via border/shape in addition to color.

advisory.note: Bracket checks are advisory (AI verdicts); the strictest chosen bracket sets this result.
